Infobox 'Established: April 1359'; 'Albanian forces, under Karl Thopia, created two new states in the southern parts of the Despotate of Epirus'; the Peter Losha page has Losha 'Despot of Arta, Rogoi and the area of Amphilochia' in 1360. The infobox month (April) is earlier than the page's late-spring date for the Battle of Achelous; the Angelokastron half is the sibling state until 1374.

ledger.note: 1374: Gjin Bua Shpata takes Arta after Losha's death and unites it with Angelokastron. Page: 'Arta and Angelokastron were united under Gjin Bua Shpata' (the infobox adds Lepanto); Gjin Bua Shpata page: 'Pjetër Losha died of the plague in Arta, after which Shpata took the city.' [Reviewer eu-05-f fix applied 2026-10-19: Nafpaktos circle subtracted.]

1376: Gjin Bua Shpata conquers Nafpaktos. Page: 'In 1376 or 1377, Shpata conquered Nafpaktos'; the page does not say who held it. The Despotate of Arta infobox lists Lepanto among the 1359-1374 predecessors, but that is a label: Nafpaktos is drawn as Spata land only from this event, and Cliopatria's shape (which contains it from 1375) is applied from 1376 (despotate-of-arta_1374 covers 1374-1375 without it). [Reviewer eu-05-f, 2026-10-19: counterpart 'unnamed holders of Nafpaktos (page silent)' replaced by catalan-company and source by the Nafpaktos page, which names the holder: 'In 1361 the town was captured by the Catalans of the Duchy of Athens'; 'In 1376 or 1377 it fell to John Bua Spata'.]

April 1378: the Hospitallers take Nafpaktos. Page: they 'captured Nafpaktos and then Vonitsa in April 1378', but Shpata 'managed to defeat and capture Heredia as a hostage' (the Grand Master also failed to take Arta, Despotate of Arta page). The page does not say how long the Hospitallers held it. [Reviewer eu-05-f, 2026-10-19: counterpart domain-of-rhodes (Leo Gabalas's lordship, 1204-1250) replaced by hospitaller-rhodes: the page names 'the Knights Hospitallers of Juan Fernandez de Heredia', the Order's state on Rhodes (1310-1522), which has no dossier yet.]

1380: Gjin Bua Shpata is master of Nafpaktos again. Page: 'he was again master of Nafpaktos by 1380'; 1380 is the latest year it allows, and the retaking may be earlier. [Reviewer eu-05-f, 2026-10-19: counterpart domain-of-rhodes (Leo Gabalas's lordship, 1204-1250) replaced by hospitaller-rhodes: the page names 'the Knights Hospitallers of Juan Fernandez de Heredia', the Order's state on Rhodes (1310-1522), which has no dossier yet.]

The year is the page's 1406 cession. [Reviewer eu-05-f, 2026-10-19: year 1407 to 1406 and counterpart house-of-tocco to ottoman-empire: the Muriq Shpata page has Pal Shpata 'in 1406 called in Ottoman assistance' and 'Paul ceded Angelokastron to the Ottomans (only for Carlo Tocco to capture it within less than a year)'; the Tocco took it from the Ottomans (house-of-tocco 1407 gain).]

wars.name: Battle of Achelous (1359)

minus.text: Arta and Aetolia, the southern Epirote lands the Albanian clans took

zones.text: Arta and Aetolia, the southern Epirote lands the Albanian clans took (the 1375 Cliopatria shape without Nafpaktos, which the Catalans held from 1361)

wars.outcome: The Albanians defeated Nikephoros II Orsini, the last Orsini despot of Epirus, and set up their two states in the south of Epirus; the battle 'won him [Losha] the rule of Arta' (Peter Losha page) and in 1360 Simeon Uros 'decided to leave the areas of Arta and Aetolia to Shpata and Losha' (Gjin Bua Shpata page).
wars.note: The page puts the battle in 'late spring 1359' and says 'The Albanians won the battle under Karl Thopia'; the Peter Losha page body gives no year (its link title says 1359) and the Epirus dossier records 1358/1359 for the battle. The contest is not opened as a ledger zone: the land passes at the founding event.

wars.name: Albanian wars with Thomas Preljubovic of Ioannina
wars.outcome: No border change: Losha's Mazaraki and Malakasi allies blockaded Ioannina in 1367-1370 (Peter Losha page); after Losha's death Shpata besieged the city, Thomas made peace by betrothing his sister Helena to Shpata, and Shpata 'again devastated the countryside of Ioannina' in May 1379; Thomas's 1380 offensive with Turkish help was beaten; Thomas was killed by his bodyguards in 1384 (Gjin Bua Shpata page).
wars.note: Ioannina lies north of the Arta shape (bbox to 39.51 N), so the front never moved on the map; the page does not date the siege to 1375.

wars.name: Hospitaller expedition to Epirus (1378)
wars.outcome: The Hospitaller Grand Master Juan Fernandez de Heredia took Nafpaktos and Vonitsa in April 1378 but was defeated and captured by Gjin Bua Shpata, who was 'again master of Nafpaktos by 1380'.
wars.note: The Despotate of Arta page says Heredia 'failed to take Arta'; it adds that Shpata then sold him to the Ottoman Turks. Vonitsa belonged to the Tocco (Leonardo I Tocco page), not to Arta.

wars.name: Tocco-Spata wars

zones.text: Arta and the rest of the Spata mainland, taken in 1416

wars.outcome: Carlo I Tocco's 1402-03 siege of Angelokastron failed and the 1406 raid into Acarnania and the Arta area did not take Arta, but Angelokastron fell to him in 1406-07; the Albanians 'almost annihilated the Tocco army' at Kranea in spring or summer 1412; Muriq died in 1414 or 1415 and Carlo took Arta in October 1416.
wars.note: Carlo is the Tocco count until February 1411 and despot of Epirus afterwards, hence the two Tocco slugs. The Despotate of Arta page: 'Muriq defeated Carlo in 1412, but the Albanians failed to take Ioannina' and 'Carlo later killed Muriq in battle in 1414-1415 and advanced on Arta'; the Carlo I Tocco page has Yaqub killed in battle in 1416. 1406 Ottoman episode: Pal Shpata called in Yusuf Beg, who was defeated. No contest zone is opened because no page says Carlo held ground in Arta before the surrender.

certainty.note: Albanian clan lordships with no treaty or survey lines; the 1360 division between Losha and Shpata and every later carve-out (Angelokastron, Naupaktos) are fortress-based and approximate. The Gulf of Corinth and the Ionian coast are natural edges.

notes:
CLIOPATRIA. The row is 1375-1421, the page's despotate is 1359-1416: the dossier starts in 1359 (infobox 'Established: April 1359', two principalities until 1374) and ends on 4 October 1416. Shapes 1375-1421 are the united Spata realm; 1359-1373 is a new keyframe (Arta half) with the Angelokastron half in the new sibling dossier despotate-of-angelokastron-and-lepanto (written in this batch, slug free in polities.csv). 1417-1421 of Cliopatria's shape is Tocco land: the Epirus dossier's 1415-1421 keyframe does not obviously contain it, so the Epirus handover in 1416 matters.

PAGES DISAGREE. (1) Rulers 1399-1403: the Despotate page lists Skurra 1399-1403 then Muriq 1403-1415; the Muriq page has Muriq at Arta from late 1399/early 1400 and Skurra at Angelokastron, Pal at Naupactus; the Gjin page has Gjin's son ruling Arta and Angelokastron for a decade. The shape is kept whole until 1407. (2) Lepanto: infobox lists it among the 1359-1374 predecessors but Gjin's page and the Nafpaktos page date Nafpaktos to 1376/77 (Catalan from 1361): drawn as Spata land from 1376 only, see the repair note. (3) Angelokastro to the Tocco: 1405 (Carlo page, 'dubious') against 1406-07 (Muriq page). (4) Muriq's death: 1414 or 1415 (Muriq page), 1414-1415 (Despotate page); Yaqub killed in battle (Carlo page) or in an ambush (Muriq page), October 1416. (5) Achelous: Losha page gives no year in the body.

NOT ON ANY PAGE OPENED. Ottoman or Serbian suzerainty: the Losha infobox says 'Despot of Arta Under the Serbian Empire 1359-1374' and Simeon Uros granted titles in 1360, but the Despotate page 'does not call the despotate a vassal'; no vassal event is written here (the serbian-empire dossier should carry a vassal_start with counterpart despotate-of-arta if its pages support it). No area figure in the infobox. Gjin's realm after 1399, the Zenebishi and Buondelmonti links, and Venice's Lepanto purchase beyond the Muriq page were not opened (page budget: five pages).

APPROXIMATE REGIONS. Angelokastron and Naupaktos are coordinate circles because the gazetteer has neither: Naupaktos 21.83 E 38.39 N 15 km (two grid cells); Angelokastron 21.2 E 38.55 N 18 km (location guessed, treat as soft); Amfilochia 21.16 E 38.86 N 15 km. Gazetteer names needed: Arta, Angelokastron, Naupactus (Lepanto), Rogoi (Filippiada), Amphilochia, Aetolia, Acarnania.

The 1378-1380 Hospitaller interval is still drawn as Spata land (two years, one town).
